places.name: Monte Albán
places.ai_summary: A UNESCO World Heritage Site featuring ancient Zapotec ruins with stunning views of the Oaxaca Valley.

opening_hours.notes: Best visited in the morning to avoid crowds.

places.place_tip: Hire a guide to learn about the history of the ruins.

places.name: Templo de Santo Domingo de Guzmán
places.ai_summary: A stunning Baroque church with intricate gold interiors and an adjacent museum showcasing Oaxaca’s rich history.

opening_hours.notes: Mass times may affect visiting hours.

places.place_tip: Visit the museum next door for a deeper understanding of Oaxaca’s culture.
places.address: Templo de Santo Domingo, Oaxaca City, Mexico

places.name: Hierve el Agua
places.ai_summary: A natural wonder featuring petrified waterfalls and mineral-rich pools, perfect for swimming and photography.

opening_hours.notes: Best visited early morning for fewer crowds.

places.place_tip: Bring a swimsuit and towel to enjoy the pools.

attribution.title: HierveElAguaMexico1

attribution.description: Hierve el Agua, a rock formation formed by mineral deposits, mainly calcium carbonate, resemble a waterfall. It is located in San Lorenzo Albarradas, Oaxaca state, Mexico.

places.name: Oaxaca Ethnobotanical Garden
places.ai_summary: A beautiful garden showcasing the diverse plant life of Oaxaca, including many species used in traditional medicine and cuisine.

opening_hours.notes: Closed on Mondays. Guided tours available.

places.place_tip: Join a guided tour to learn about the medicinal plants.

attribution.usage_terms: Creative Commons Zero, Public Domain Dedication

places.name: Museo de las Culturas de Oaxaca
places.ai_summary: A museum housed in a former convent, featuring exhibits on the history and culture of Oaxaca, including pre-Hispanic artifacts.

opening_hours.notes: Closed on Mondays. Check for temporary exhibitions.

places.place_tip: Don't miss the pre-Hispanic gold jewelry exhibit.
places.address: Museo de las Culturas, Oaxaca City, Mexico

places.name: Zócalo Oaxaca
places.ai_summary: The main square of Oaxaca City, surrounded by historic buildings, shops, and restaurants. A great place to experience the local culture.

opening_hours.notes: Always open, but best visited in the evening.

places.place_tip: Enjoy a coffee at one of the terrace cafés.

attribution.description: Graffitis by protesters on walls of Oaxaca Juarez

places.name: Mercado Benito Juárez
places.ai_summary: A traditional market in Oaxaca City, offering a wide variety of local products, handicrafts, and food. A great place to buy souvenirs.

opening_hours.notes: Best visited in the morning for fresh produce.

places.place_tip: Try the local cheese and mezcal.
places.address: Mercado Benito Juárez, Oaxaca City, Mexico

attribution.title: Ciudad Juárez, skyline
attribution.author: Alejandro Rosales
attribution.description: Panorámica urbana del norte de Ciudad Juárez; en primer plano el centro histórico y al fondo la zona Paseo Triunfo de la República.

places.name: Teotitlán del Valle Weaving Village
places.ai_summary: A village near Oaxaca City, famous for its traditional Zapotec weaving. Visit local workshops and learn about this ancient craft.

opening_hours.notes: Best visited on weekdays to avoid crowds.

places.place_tip: Purchase a handmade rug directly from the weavers.

places.name: Mitla Archaeological Site
places.ai_summary: An important archaeological site in Oaxaca, known for its unique Mitla-style architecture and intricate stone mosaics.

opening_hours.notes: Best visited in the late afternoon for sunset views.

places.place_tip: Explore the site with a guide to understand its history.

places.name: San Bartolo Coyotepec Pottery Village
places.ai_summary: A village famous for its black pottery, where you can visit workshops and see artisans at work.

opening_hours.notes: Best visited on weekends to see the artisans.

places.place_tip: Buy directly from the artisans for the best prices.

attribution.title: Cancun aerial photo by safa
attribution.author: Safa in la but uploaded by Mardetanha

places.name: Tlacolula Market
places.ai_summary: A vibrant local market held every Sunday in Tlacolula, offering a wide range of products from fresh produce to handicrafts.

opening_hours.notes: Only open on Sundays. Arrive early for the best selection.

places.place_tip: Try the tlayudas and mezcal.

places.name: Church of San Felipe Neri
places.ai_summary: A beautiful church in Oaxaca City, known for its stunning altar and religious art.

opening_hours.notes: Mass times may affect visiting hours.

places.place_tip: Admire the altar and the religious paintings.
places.address: San Felipe Neri, Oaxaca City, Mexico

places.name: Mercado 20 de Noviembre
places.ai_summary: A bustling market in Oaxaca City, known for its food stalls and local products. A great place to experience the local cuisine.

opening_hours.notes: Best visited in the morning for fresh food.

places.place_tip: Try the mole and tamales.
places.address: Mercado 20 de Noviembre, Oaxaca City, Mexico

places.name: Museo Rufino Tamayo
places.ai_summary: An art museum in Oaxaca City, featuring a collection of pre-Hispanic art and artifacts, as well as works by Mexican artist Rufino Tamayo.

opening_hours.notes: Closed on Mondays. Check for temporary exhibitions.

places.place_tip: Look for the temporary exhibitions for unique artworks.
places.address: Museo Rufino Tamayo, Oaxaca City, Mexico

places.name: Yagul Ruins
places.ai_summary: The archaeological site of Yagul features impressive ruins and offers stunning views of the surrounding valley.

opening_hours.notes: Best visited in the late afternoon for sunset views.

places.place_tip: Bring water and wear comfortable shoes.

places.name: El Tule Tree
places.ai_summary: A famous Montezuma cypress tree located in the town of Santa María del Tule, near Oaxaca City. It's known for its massive trunk circumference.

opening_hours.notes: Always open. Best visited in the morning.

places.place_tip: Take a photo with the tree to appreciate its size.
places.address: Santa María del Tule, Oaxaca, Mexico

places.name: Andador Macedonio Alcalá Street
places.ai_summary: A pedestrian walkway in Oaxaca City, lined with shops, galleries, and restaurants. It's a great place to experience the local culture and cuisine.

opening_hours.notes: Always open. Best visited in the evening.

places.place_tip: Enjoy dinner at a rooftop restaurant for a view of the sunset.
places.address: Andador Macedonio Alcalá, Oaxaca City, Mexico

places.name: Mezcal Distillery Tours
places.ai_summary: Tours of local mezcal distilleries where you can learn about the production of this traditional Oaxacan spirit and enjoy tastings.

opening_hours.notes: Advance booking recommended for tours.

places.place_tip: Buy a bottle of mezcal directly from the distillery.

places.name: Textile Museum of Oaxaca
places.ai_summary: A museum dedicated to the textile arts of Oaxaca, featuring a collection of traditional and contemporary textiles.

opening_hours.notes: Closed on Mondays. Check for temporary exhibitions.

places.place_tip: Look for the weaving demonstrations.

places.name: San Pablo Cultural Center
places.ai_summary: A cultural center in Oaxaca City, offering art exhibitions, workshops, and a café. A great place to relax and enjoy local art.

opening_hours.notes: Closed on Mondays. Check for current exhibitions.

places.place_tip: Enjoy a coffee at the café and browse the art shop.
places.address: San Pablo Cultural Center, Oaxaca City, Mexico
